narrative.overview:
Game Backlog is a calm desk where the plan sits. The surfaces are quiet paper on a cool grey desk, the lines between them are thin rules, and the numbers line up like a ledger: tabular figures, right-aligned hours, dates as dd.mm.yyyy. One blue says what is current and what moves the plan; everything else stays in ink and grey. The product replaced a spreadsheet, and the system keeps that honesty: density serves scanning, and nothing animates for show.

The mood is calm, precise, unhurried. This is a restrained Operate-mode product UI: a sticky top bar, a Now playing card at the peak of the page, then tables that hold the whole plan in view at 1280×820 and still work at 900×600. Below 900px, the web app on a phone, the same page folds into one column: the tables become stacked rows and every control grows to a fingertip's size, with no second visual language. The accent is rare, hover is a tint rather than a lift, and depth is ambient (a soft shadow under cards, a popover shadow for things that float) rather than structural. Light and dark themes share one grammar; in dark the washes deepen and the accents lighten so dark ink can sit on them.

The confirmed anti-reference is "a generic admin table": grey chrome with no point of view. The build answers it with the Now playing hero (an accent wash, the cover at full weight, the title at full strength), the six Design chips, the dotted status words and the ledger numbers; these are what make the system read as this product rather than any dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, Plan Blue, reserved for action, selection and the current game.
Paper surfaces on a cool grey desk with 1px rules; no colored stripes or side borders.
One family (system-ui), six fixed pixel steps, tabular numerals everywhere a number is compared.
Ambient elevation: a soft shadow at rest on cards and the Now playing card, a popover shadow only for things that float, flat tables.
Nested radii: 12px containers, 8px controls, 6px small controls, 14px dialogs, pills for chips and counts.
The only entrance animation is the Now playing handover, and it never runs on first paint.
One page at every width: columns leave as the window narrows, below 900px the tables fold into stacked rows, and nothing ever scrolls sideways.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Plan Blue marks exactly three things: an action that moves the plan, a selected control, and the current game. Headings, chrome, icons and dividers stay in ink and grey; if a screen shows blue anywhere else, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Dark Ink Rule
rules.body: Every filled color carries its own `--on-*` text token. In light theme that text is white; in dark theme the fills lighten and the text flips to dark ink (`#0f1216`). Never hard-code white on a fill.

rules.name: The Soft Pair Rule
rules.body: A semantic color appears either as a fill with `--on-*` text, or as its wash carrying the same role's colored text (error banner, dropped pill, danger-ghost hover). It is never used as a border stripe or an outline on its own.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: system-ui is the only face. No webfont, no display face, no monospace; alignment comes from tabular numerals and right-aligned cells.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Any number that will be compared down a column (hours, dates, counts, ratings, stat values) is set with `tabular-nums`; in tables it is right-aligned and never wraps.

rules.name: The Fixed Steps Rule
rules.body: Six pixel sizes (11/12/13/14/18/22), no fluid or clamp sizes. Under 1400px only numbers and dates step down to 13px and chip padding tightens; chips and status words keep the 12px caption size, and 11px stays reserved for uppercase labels.

rules.name: The One Window Rule
rules.body: There is no max-width container and no sidebar; the plan table is the page at every width. Narrowing drops columns (at 1240px and 1160px) instead of wrapping cells, below 900px the tables fold into stacked rows, and at no width does the page scroll sideways.

rules.name: The Folded Ledger Rule
rules.body: Below 900px each game is one stacked row: line one holds the drag handle, number, title and actions; line two the Design chip, status word and hours (with "h"); line three the date range (on a finished game, its review). What a narrow window hides stays hidden. The header row is hidden from view only, and the tables carry explicit table, row, header and cell roles, so a screen reader still hears each cell's column.

rules.name: The Fingertip Rule
rules.body: On a touch phone (below 900px with a coarse pointer) every control is at least 40px tall: icon buttons are 40px square with 6px between a row's actions, small buttons become full buttons, the drag handle and the theme options are 32×40, and a link inside a line of text (a title, Rate, the plan's two values) answers 10px above and below instead of making the line taller. A narrow window with a mouse keeps desktop density.

rules.name: The Short Window Rule
rules.body: Under 700px of window height the Now playing card gives rows back: `12px 16px` padding, a 56×75 cover, a Headline title, and no meta line or explanation note; nothing else changes.

rules.name: The Sticky Ledger Rule
rules.body: The top bar (52px) and the table headers stay fixed while rows scroll; nothing else is sticky. (Below 900px the header row is out of view, so only the top bar stays.)

rules.name: The One Stop Rule
rules.body: A composite control is one Tab stop. A table row lands on its title and the theme switch on its chosen option; Left/Right (and Home/End) move inside, and a row remembers the control it left. The skip links sit before the top bar, so the first Tab on the page reaches the finished games or the stats.

rules.name: The Ambient Rule
rules.body: Shadows describe where a surface sits, never where attention should go. Resting surfaces get Ambient, floating surfaces get Popover, dialogs get Dialog; no element gets a hard or colored shadow, and nothing gains a shadow on hover.

rules.name: The Tint-Not-Lift Rule
rules.body: Every hover is a background tint (Paper Shade for controls, Paper Hover for rows, the role's wash for ghost danger and success icons) with a 120ms ease; no transform, no shadow change.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: A control inside a container is one step tighter than the container: 12px wrapper, 8px control, 6px inner control. Dialogs sit one step looser at 14px.

rules.name: The Thin Line Rule
rules.body: Every border is 1px and grey; a role color may tint a border only through `color-mix` with the grey or the transparent base, never as a solid colored edge or side stripe.

rules.name: The Typed Date Rule
rules.body: A date is read and written the same way everywhere: dd.mm.yyyy text with the picker one click away. No surface shows a bare native date input or a month-first order.

rules.name: The Second Chance Rule
rules.body: An undo offer lasts 20 seconds and says so. The clock is a draining track and a count, not a toast that vanishes; it waits while the pointer or focus is on the notice, and the notice takes focus when it appears so the offer is the next thing a keyboard reaches.

rules.name: The Edit Where You Read Rule
rules.body: A number that moves the plan is edited where its effect is read. Settings keeps the same field, but the card owns the moment, and saving there recalculates every date at once.

rules.name: The Handover Rule
rules.body: When the current game changes after mount, the cover and body enter with `now-enter`: 400ms `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, opacity 0→1 and an 8px rise. The first paint never animates. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the entrance is a 200ms fade; the finished-row settle shortens from 1600ms to 800ms and control transitions are removed.

rules.name: The Dot Not Pill Rule
rules.body: Status is a word with a dot. Only "Dropped" and the "Today" marker are pills, and no status gets a colored border.

dos: Do draw every icon with the `Icon` component: a 24-unit grid, 2px round-capped strokes in `currentColor`, 16px by default, `aria-hidden`, with the surrounding control carrying the accessible name.
Do keep Plan Blue for action, selection and the current game (The One Blue Rule) and give every fill its `--on-*` text token so dark theme flips to dark ink.
Do set compared numbers in `tabular-nums`, right-aligned in tables, and dates as dd.mm.yyyy.
Do write labels in sentence case at 12px/600; reserve uppercase 11px tracking for table headers and search section names.
Do make hover a one-step tint with a 120ms ease and focus a 2px Plan Blue outline offset 2px (inset 2px inside menus).
Do nest radii: 12px container, 8px control, 6px small control, 14px dialog, pills for chips and counts.
Do give floating surfaces the Popover shadow and resting surfaces the Ambient shadow; keep tables flat inside their wrapper.
Do keep the current game's row on Current Row Wash under hover, and let row actions brighten from Ink Muted to Ink on hover or focus-within.
Do name the empty state's fact and its next step in a dashed 12px panel with one button.
Do make a row and a segmented control one Tab stop, with Left/Right moving inside, and keep the skip links before the top bar.
Do take every date as dd.mm.yyyy text through `DateField`, with the native picker behind its calendar button.
Do show an undo offer's clock (a draining track and a count) and pause it while the notice is hovered or focused.
Do give every control on a touch phone at least 40px, or a 10px taller hit area for a link inside a line of text (The Fingertip Rule); keep desktop density for a mouse.
Do keep a restyled table a table for screen readers: a header row hidden from view only, and explicit table, row, header and cell roles.
donts: Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons; every icon is an inline SVG from the set.
Don't add colored side borders, left stripes or solid colored edges to rows, cards, banners or chips; role color enters a border only through `color-mix`.
Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings; a section is a Headline, optionally with a count pill.
Don't animate on page load, stagger entrances or add page-load choreography; the only entrance is the Now playing handover after a change.
Don't load a webfont, a display face or a monospace face; system-ui is the one family.
Don't use hard offset shadows, colored shadows or hover lifts; depth is ambient and hover is a tint.
Don't hard-code white text on an accent or semantic fill; use the `--on-*` token.
Don't render status as a colored pill or badge (except "Dropped"); it is a word with a dot.
Don't rename the "Design" chips or their six fixed color pairs.
Don't add a max-width container or a sidebar, and never let the page scroll sideways: columns drop at 1240px and 1160px, and below 900px the tables fold into stacked rows.
Don't show a bare native date input or let a date read month-first; `DateField` wraps the picker.
Don't make every row action its own Tab stop; the row is the stop and arrows move inside it.
